name: budget_day_strategy_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Union Budget day (typically Feb 1) is the single highest-volatility scheduled event in Indian markets. The budget speech starts at 11:00 IST and runs for 90-120 minutes. The intraday pattern: (1) 09:15-11:00: pre-speech compression with low volume, (2) 11:00-12:30: sector-specific knee-jerk reactions as tax changes, capex allocations, and subsidy announcements are read out, (3) 12:30-15:30: digestion and reversion of overreactions. The key insight: sector-specific reactions during the speech (e.g., infrastructure capex increase → infra stocks spike) overshoot by 30-50% because retail traders act on headlines without reading details. By 14:00, as analysts digest the full budget, partial reversion occurs. The strategy: identify sector winners/losers during the speech, then fade the extreme movers after 12:30.
stock_filter: Focus on sectors historically affected by budget: Infra, Defence, Pharma, Auto, FMCG, Tobacco, Real Estate, Banking
session: 12:30-15:15 IST (budget day only — post-speech reversion phase)

conditions: sector_reaction_rank >= 8 (bottom 3 sectors — biggest losers during speech)
sector_reaction_rank <= 2 (top 2 sectors — biggest winners during speech)

exit.target: 30-50% reversion of speech reaction (e.g., if lost 200 bps, target 60-100 bps recovery)
exit.stop_loss: reaction extends by 50% beyond speech extreme (e.g., if lost 200 bps, stop at 300 bps loss)
exit.trailing_stop: 20 bps trailing after 30 bps reversion achieved
exit.signal_exit: vix_change_budget > +5 (panic mode, all sectors selling, no reversion)

risk.position_sizing: ₹75K per trade (reduced due to budget day extreme volatility)

filters.vix_filter: no VIX filter on budget day (VIX will be elevated by definition)
filters.time_filter: entry only in 12:30-13:30 window; exit by 15:15
filters.volume_filter: sector stocks trading at > 2x normal volume (confirms interest)
filters.trend_filter: fade extreme sector movers (contrarian by design)
filters.spread_filter: bid-ask < 20 bps (wider tolerance on budget day)
filters.event_filter: ONLY on budget day (1 per year)
other_filters: skip sectors where budget impact is structural, not cyclical (e.g., new tax on tobacco is permanent, not overreaction)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Very Low — budget day happens once per year and the overreaction/reversion pattern is robust because retail emotional reactions to fiscal policy announcements are deeply behavioral.

weaknesses: Only 1 trade day per year. The strategy's contribution to annual P&L is minimal unless the edge per trade is very large (~50 bps) and size is scaled up.
Distinguishing structural budget changes (new tax, sector deregulation) from cyclical allocations (higher capex for one year) is qualitative and hard to automate.
Slippage on budget day is extreme — true slippage may be 10-20 bps, not 3 bps. The edge math assumes normal slippage which is unrealistic.
prior_art: Cutler, Poterba & Summers (1989) 'What Moves Stock Prices?' — event-driven returns. In India, Gupta & Kundu (2006) study budget day stock market reactions. Mohanty (2013) analyzes fiscal policy impact on Indian equity sectors.
notes: This is the single highest expected-bps strategy in the portfolio but also the lowest frequency. Consider using options for leverage on budget day: buy sector ETF options to limit downside while capturing the reversion. Historical budget day sector returns (available from NSE) provide a useful calibration dataset.
